title: Printable Islamic pattern construction sheet (lesson 62)
subject: Mathematics
unit: Summer 1: Geometric notation and constructions; geometric reasoning
source: Seeded from mathematics/y7 lesson 62 (Printable Islamic pattern construction sheet (portal worksheet for this lesson; usable on a drawing tablet))
intro: Lesson 62: Constructions in Islamic geometric patterns. To understand how compass constructions create regular hexagons, stars and Islamic geometric patterns

model.title: Construct a regular hexagon in a circle of radius 4 cm.

parts.label: Step 1
parts.text: Draw a circle of radius 4 cm and mark a point on it

parts.label: Step 2
parts.text: Keep the radius: step round the circle, marking 6 points

parts.label: Step 3
parts.text: Join neighbouring points with a ruler

questions.q: Construct a regular hexagon with sides of 5 cm.
questions.a: Circle of radius 5 cm; step 6 points round it; join them
questions.model: Draw a circle of radius 5 cm. Keep the compasses at 5 cm and step round, marking six points. Join neighbouring points with a ruler.

questions.q: Two 60° angles meet at each corner of the hexagon. What is its interior angle?
Join alternate vertices of the hexagon. What shape do you get?
(a) construct a regular hexagon in a circle of radius 5 cm (b) draw the six-point star (c) shade it in two colours to keep its symmetry and write its order of rotational symmetry.
questions.a: (a) sides of 5 cm (b) two overlapping equilateral triangles (c) order 6
questions.model: (a) Mark one point on the circle; keep the compasses at 5 cm and step round; join neighbouring points. (b) Join alternate points to make one triangle, then the other three.

questions.q: Bisect the angles at the centre to make 12 equal parts. What angle is each part?
Regular hexagons tessellate. Use angles to explain why.
questions.a: Each interior angle is 120°, and three meet at a point: 3 × 120° = 360°.

questions.q: The side of a hexagon drawn this way equals the:
Order of rotational symmetry of a six-point star
Big question: how did craftsmen build these patterns with only compasses and a straight edge?
questions.a: Stepping the radius round a circle makes six equal parts; joining and bisecting builds hexagons, stars and twelve-fold patterns.
